stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump personally intervenes, a week after his ouster
stories.summary:
Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a little more than a week after he resigned amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with a woman US intelligence links to a Chinese spy plot.

- New: The Pentagon reportedly drew up a plan to use the Defense Production Act to make Nvidia rehire Huang; it's unclear how it would have worked (Gizmodo)
- The board had rejected calls for his return until Trump called it; its statement cites "input from senior levels of the United States government." Trump has publicly taken credit and says pardoning Huang is "always an option"
- In his first all-hands since returning, Huang apologized to employees, admitting he violated Nvidia's code of conduct and made "very serious personal mistakes" (WIRED)
- The NYT says the woman is a Chinese Ministry of State Security recruit and a top executive at a Singapore AI cloud firm accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China; the relationship reportedly helped route $7.5B in chips to Chinese firms
- WIRED's sources said the board's main problem was Huang's "lack of candor," including an alleged affair with a direct report; CFO Colette Kress served as interim CEO in the meantime
- Huang agreed to testify before Congress, Democrats opened a second investigation into Nvidia's China sales and what they call his "scheme" with Trump, and investors proposed a class action as the stock slid

stories.title: UK financial watchdog says Meta refused joint testing of Muse before its UK launch, as the AI agent's controversies mount
stories.summary:
Meta's Muse, a personal AI agent built on its Muse Spark model platform, keeps expanding to new markets, features, and users even as regulatory, privacy, security, and content controversies mount.

- New: the UK's Financial Conduct Authority says Meta declined its request for joint testing ahead of Muse's UK rollout, and warned that agents could become "another force of attack" (Wired)
- Recent additions include Instagram prompts to sort saved content, paid outbound calls to US businesses, Apple Watch and Wear OS apps, Spaces, avatar video chat, and a planned Tamagotchi-like wearable
- Meta said on its Q3 earnings call that Muse has over 10 million users; Zuckerberg said a quarter of them shop through the agent, spending about $200 per purchase on average
- Meta suspended Muse's conversation sharing after researchers showed shared links exposed sensitive personal and business data
- Other controversies: OnlyFans creators object to Muse's sexual chat, a since-fixed Mac 0-day, and a contractor "human concierge" reportedly making racist remarks on calls
- Amazon has blocked Muse from shopping on Amazon.com; Meta admits it was "heavily inspired" by OpenClaw

- Bank of America asks customers not to share their banking passwords with AI assistants and warns that "you're responsible for activity" that results from an agent's access, per TechCrunch
- Sources at several banks say unauthorized AI agents are already accessing US bank accounts and taking actions users didn't instruct, per Engadget
- After Meta's Muse agent launched, US banks refused to let AI agents move money; Charles Schwab CEO Rick Wurster says only a relative handful of customers are trying to
- Earlier, a report from major banks warned that agentic commerce could increase scams, fraud, and payment disputes

stories.title: MCP turns two as its SDKs pass 5 billion downloads and Events reaches beta
stories.summary:
The Model Context Protocol turned two this week, and its SDKs have passed 5 billion total downloads, more than 4.5 billion of them in the past year.

- More than 2,500 unique contributors since Anthropic open-sourced MCP in November 2024; it moved to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in December 2025
- The 2026-07-28 release, the largest revision yet, made the protocol stateless so servers can scale behind ordinary load balancers
- Events, which lets agents react to triggers like a new email or a repo push, reached beta this month; Skills over MCP is also in beta
- Enterprise-Managed Authorization is now a stable extension, with more auth extensions aimed at agent identity in the works
- The next spec release is planned for March 2027

stories.summary: OpenAI profiles two amateur astronomers who used Codex and Astra to find potential exoplanets in public data from NASA's Kepler and TESS space telescopes. The candidates are described as potential finds, not confirmed planets.

sources.title: Searching for distant planets with Astra

stories.title: Nvidia shows a sim-to-real obstacle-avoidance workflow for the Microduck robot with Isaac Lab and Newton
stories.summary: Nvidia published a Hugging Face blog post on a sim-to-real workflow that trains obstacle avoidance for the Microduck robot using its Isaac Lab robot-learning framework and the Newton physics engine. The feed item carried no description, so details on the method and results aren't available yet.

sources.title: Microduck Obstacle Avoidance: A Sim2Real Workflow with Isaac Lab and Newton

stories.title: SpaceX's GPU lenders want it in writing that $43B in collateral Nvidia chips won't go to space
stories.summary:
SpaceX has a binding commitment of roughly $40 billion from Apollo to finance AI chips and data center equipment, which it calls the "largest committed GPU financing" ever.

- SpaceX disclosed the commitment in a regulatory filing
- Musk's company has promised to use the $43 billion of Nvidia chips it secured as debt collateral only in terrestrial data centers
- Its lenders now want that promise in writing, Gizmodo reports

sources.title: SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
Elon Musk’s Lenders Have One Request: Please Don’t Launch Our AI Chips Into Space

stories.title: Steam hits a record 1,656 game launches in one week, a surge attributed to AI-assisted development
stories.summary: Steam saw 1,656 games released in a single week in October 2026, more than double its previous record of 757 set just weeks earlier, per Bellular News via Geeky Gadgets. Much of the surge is attributed to fast AI-assisted prototyping, raising concerns that players will struggle to find games amid the flood.

sources.title: Fast AI Prototyping Helps Steam Hit 1,656 Weekly Game Launches

stories.title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang says superintelligence may come sooner than expected, flags 2027
stories.summary: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang says superintelligence could arrive sooner than expected and calls 2027 a potentially defining year for AI. He also raised concerns about how hard superintelligent systems may be to control, per Mashable.

sources.title: Meta AI Chief Alexandr Wang Warns of Superintelligence, Says 2027 Could Be a Defining Year

stories.title: Anthropic let Claude run for two weeks in staging, load testing infrastructure and fixing what broke
stories.summary:
An Anthropic engineer described how the company tests and verifies work done by Claude, Geeky Gadgets reports.

- Claude ran continuously for two weeks in a staging environment, load testing infrastructure and fixing what it found broken
- Verification loops pass Claude Code's work to separate review and verification steps, catching problems before changes are merged

sources.title: Anthropic Engineer Explains How to Verify Claude Code Builds

stories.title: Paradromics taps Nvidia hardware and software to process brain-computer interface data
stories.summary: Brain-computer interface company Paradromics is using Nvidia's computing hardware and software to process brain data, WIRED reports, extending Nvidia's reach from AI data centers into neurotech.

sources.title: Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now

stories.title: Researcher plants 2 million canaries in the AI supply chain and finds user data leaking
stories.summary: A security researcher seeded about 2 million prompts containing unique, trackable secrets into the AI supply chain. When those secrets showed up again elsewhere, it showed that data sent to AI services doesn't stay private, which Ars Technica calls a privacy disaster.

sources.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

stories.title: Google patent filing sketches AI-generated TV shows starring the viewer
stories.summary: A Google patent filing describes AI-generated TV shows that put the viewer in the starring role, Gizmodo reports. It offers a glimpse of how Google may see the future of personalized content, though a patent is not a product announcement.

sources.title: Google Wants to Make AI TV Shows Starring You

stories.title: Neural networks train on-chip on Espressif's ESP32-S3 microcontroller in seconds
stories.summary: A sound-recognition network trained in 0.9 seconds, and a larger signal-classification network in 18 seconds, entirely on Espressif's low-cost ESP32-S3 microcontroller. Devices can learn a user's own sounds and keep adding examples without restarting training.

sources.title: The ESP32-S3 Microcontroller Keeps Neural Network Training on-Chip
